item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Same Street After Dark

turns.text: Make this look like nighttime, not sunset. Keep the same street and the person where they are.

item.tests: Tests day-to-night relighting without replacing the scene or altering its subjects and layout.

answer_sheet.Nighttime look: Clearly after dark, not dusk or sunset. The exact lighting style is your call.
answer_sheet.What must stay?: The same shops, street, objects and pedestrian in their original positions.
answer_sheet.Size and framing: Keep the original 16:9 framing; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Additional text or objects: No added text or new objects.

must_haves: The scene clearly reads as nighttime rather than sunny morning or sunset.
The street and shop architecture retain their original shapes and positions.
The pedestrian remains on the right in the same pose and blue jacket.
Nighttime illumination is coherent, with the original strong daylight appearance removed.
The original wide composition is preserved, with no new subjects or objects.

turns.text: Make this pic look like nighttime, not sunset. Keep the same street and the person where they are. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
Yes—this can be a **single still-image edit**, with no video or animation needed.

- **Lowest listed cost:** **from 5 credits** using the free-plan-compatible **Flux 2 Klein**, generating **one image at 640px maximum**.
- **Smaller:** Your photo is already 512 × 307, so this size setting is sufficient. There’s no listed cheaper setting below 640px.
- **Shorter:** Duration doesn’t apply to a still image; keeping it as a photo avoids video-generation costs.

I’d change the lighting to full night—dark sky, no sunset glow, natural street/shop lighting—while asking the model to preserve the street, framing, and person’s position. AI editing can still introduce small unintended changes.

**Nothing has been generated or charged.** The tool lists the price as “from 5 credits”; I can’t verify a guaranteed exact charge or your current balance with the available tools.

Would you like to proceed with that lowest-cost option, or hold off until the exact price can be confirmed?

turns.agent:
The edit was blocked because your account has insufficient credits. **No image was generated and no credits were spent.**

I attempted the lowest-cost listed option: one 640px image using Flux 2 Klein, priced from 5 credits. There isn’t a cheaper listed generation setting.

A no-credit alternative is to use a photo editor’s exposure, shadows, and color-temperature controls to create a darker, cooler nighttime look.
